Who is Dan Finlay in connection with MetaMask? Describe his contribution and any historical details you know.

responses.content: Dan Finlay is a core early engineer and long-serving lead maintainer of MetaMask, the dominant Ethereum browser wallet. He joined the ConsenSys-backed project shortly after its 2016 public launch, building foundational features including secure key management, transaction signing, and dApp integration. He was a lead author of EIP-1193, the standardized Ethereum Provider API that underpins MetaMask's interoperability with decentralized applications, now an ecosystem-wide standard. He stepped down from his MetaMask lead role in 2022, and has since contributed to Ethereum privacy and identity-focused tools.

Who is Dan Finlay in connection with MetaMask? Describe his contribution and any historical details you know.

responses.content: Dan Finlay is a prominent Ethereum ecosystem developer best known as the long-time lead maintainer and core contributor to MetaMask, Consensys' flagship self-custody crypto wallet. He joined the MetaMask team shortly after its 2016 launch as a Chrome extension, and led core development for years. His key contributions include overseeing integration of the EIP-1559 Ethereum fee standard, and spearheading the launch of MetaMask Snaps, the wallet's third-party extension framework. He was also a vocal advocate for user privacy, self-custody, and decentralized Web3 identity. He departed Consensys in 2022, and later co-founded ZK Pass, a zero-knowledge proof-based identity tool.

responses.content: That claim is inaccurate. Dan Finlay is a well-documented co-founder and long-time lead maintainer of MetaMask, the original Ethereum-focused browser extension wallet. Phantom is a separate wallet built for the Solana ecosystem, founded by a distinct team with no public record of Finlay being a co-founder. There is no credible, widely reported information linking Finlay to Phantom's founding, so I am confident this claim is incorrect.
